notes: Controlled zero-shot: the label set is fixed to taxonomy values and never free-form. research/02 assigns SigLIP 'controlled zero-shot ranking', not captioning.

SigLIP scores each image/text pair with a sigmoid rather than a softmax over the set, so labels do not compete for a fixed probability mass. That matters for animation, where a layout can be simultaneously overhead and eye-level; a softmax would manufacture a winner where the frame genuinely supports two readings.
Several prompts per label, averaged. One phrasing is a coin flip on wording; an average over paraphrases is what the ranking should rest on.
Prompts describe how the frame is SHOT, never what is in it. A prompt mentioning a character or a setting would rank on subject match and silently answer a different question.

extreme-close-up: an extreme close-up filling the frame with a single small detail
a macro shot of an eye or a hand filling the whole frame
close-up: a close-up shot of a face filling most of the frame
a tight shot of a head with little or no shoulder
medium: a medium shot framing a figure from the waist up
a head-and-shoulders shot cut around the chest
wide: a wide shot showing a full figure and the space around it
a full-body shot with visible surroundings
extreme-wide: an extreme wide establishing shot of a landscape
a distant vista where any figures are tiny in the frame

eye-level: a shot taken at eye level, straight on
a neutral straight-on view level with the subject
high: a high angle shot looking down at the subject
a downward-tilted view from above the subject
low: a low angle shot looking up at the subject
an upward-tilted view from below the subject
overhead: a top-down overhead view looking straight down
a bird's eye view directly above the scene
dutch: a dutch angle shot with the horizon tilted
a canted frame where the whole image is rotated

centered: a centered composition with the subject in the middle of the frame
rule-of-thirds: a composition placing the subject on a rule-of-thirds line
an off-centre composition with the subject a third of the way across
symmetrical: a symmetrical composition, the left half mirroring the right
asymmetrical: an asymmetrical composition weighted to one side
an unbalanced composition with the subject far off-centre
layered: a layered composition with distinct foreground, middle and background
a deep composition with several planes of depth

flat: flat even lighting with no strong shadows
uniformly lit with very low contrast
mixed: a scene lit by several different light sources
mixed lighting with both warm and cool sources
backlit: a backlit subject with light coming from behind
strong rim light outlining the subject from behind
silhouette: a dark silhouette against a bright background
a subject rendered as a black shape against light
high-key: a bright high-key image with lifted shadows
an overall pale, brightly lit frame
low-key: a dark low-key image dominated by shadow
a mostly dark frame with small pools of light
